note: Seed transcript of session 1 (Kladno childhood, unfinished story of the fair in Prague). Odd turns = GRANDPA, even = TOM. The opener (session.firstMessage) was spoken before t01.
firstMessage: Hi Grandpa, it's me, Tom. I'd love to hear about when you were little. Where did you grow up?
turns: grandparent
Well, in Kladno, of course. I was born there in forty-six, in 1946, and I grew up in a street just by the Poldi steelworks. We could see the chimneys from our window.
ai
The Poldi chimneys right outside your window, I can picture that. Who in your family worked there?
grandparent
My dad, František, worked at the Poldi steelworks, at the furnace. When he went off to his shift in the morning you could hear his boots all down the street. He came home black as a chimney sweep.
ai
Your dad František at the furnace, that must have been hard work. And what was your mum like?
grandparent
My mum was called Anna. She baked buns with plum jam, oh, that smell, it drifted all the way out to the yard. On Sundays we fought over them.
ai
Buns with plum jam, that sounds lovely. Did you have any brothers or sisters?
grandparent
Well, yes, that's a long story, that would take a while.
ai
Take your time, Grandpa. Were you the oldest?
grandparent
I was. Then my sister Věrka came along. Věrka and I were always squabbling, but when things got tough, we stuck together like one.
ai
That's lovely that you stuck together. Who did you play with most outside?
grandparent
Outside? We were always outside, on the patch behind the house. There was a whole gang of boys from the street.
ai
A whole gang of boys on the patch. Did you have a best friend among them?
grandparent
Pepa. Pepa Dvořák. He lived next door and he was two years younger than me, but that didn't matter, he was a boy you could count on.
ai
Pepa Dvořák from next door, two years younger. What did you like doing together most?
grandparent
We played football on the patch until it got dark. Then Mum would shout from the window for me to come home. And Pepa and I cooked up all sorts of mischief.
ai
What kind of mischief did you and Pepa cook up?
grandparent

Well, once in fifty-eight, that was in 1958, Pepa and I ran off to the fair in Prague. No money, just like that, on the train without tickets. But how we got home and what my dad said about it, well, I'll tell you next time, my throat's sore now.
ai
Oh, I can't wait for that, Grandpa, I won't forget. Thank you for today.
